Telemetry & Physics Guide

Energy Conservation |ΔE/E₀|

In gravitational N-body simulations, total energy E = K + U must remain invariant over time.

AL-BH employs the Kick-Drift-Kick (KDK) Leapfrog scheme, a symplectic integrator that preserves phase space volume:

ΔE / E₀ < 0.1% → Excellent Symplectic Bounded Drift

Virial Theorem (2K/|U|)

For a self-gravitating spherical stellar system (e.g. Plummer model) in dynamic equilibrium:

2 ⟨K⟩ + ⟨U⟩ = 0 &implies; 2K / |U| ≈ 1.00

If started cold (2K/|U| < 1), the cluster undergoes gravitational collapse before virializing through phase mixing.

Barnes–Hut Force vs. Tree Build

Traditional direct N-body requires O(N²) pairwise interactions. Barnes–Hut reduces this to O(N log N) by clustering distant nodes with opening criterion:

s / d < θ (where θ = 0.5)

The linearized array-based Octree ensures tree construction takes only < 15% of step time, while force traversal dominates without cache thrashing.

MPI Domain Imbalance Ratio

Defined as I = T_max / T_avg across all MPI ranks.

Without dynamic load balancing, dense cluster centers cause extreme imbalance (I > 20x). AL-BH's Morton space-filling curve partitions and adaptive boundary migration restore I ≈ 1.00x.
